_note: Batch 13. Seven cards, seven posts, read from the 27 remaining candidates rather than taken on score. Spread deliberately: 3850 has ZERO cards, 3879 and 4008 have one each. Cut on the read, with reasons: 3978's two chest-pain sections are still tabled in '4 Key Differences' (fifth time), 3796 and 2780 likewise; 3894's 'Don't Second-Guess Your Heart Health' is a call to action; 3921's pediatric-care section describes the facility; 3879's 'What an ER Can Do That a Pharmacy Cannot' turned out to be facility feature bullets (experienced physicians, on-site labs, open 24/7) rather than a decision; 3081's two X-ray sections largely duplicate each other and the items are generic ('digestive issues', 'urinary tract complications'), which is the answered-elsewhere pattern the detector misses when neither section carries a table; 3875's 'What to Expect During Your Visit' is 561 characters of prose and a phone number with nothing to enumerate; 3979's numbered sub-emergencies are already covered by that post's overview card; 3097's differential list is a clinician rule-out, not a patient decision. Held rather than cut: 3825's dog-bite closure section is genuinely good but the decision is the doctor's, and 3977, 3091, 3803, 3365 are all process sections on posts that already carry three or more cards.

cards.subject: Pharmacy
cards.heading: Signs You Need a Doctor Right Now
title: When to
Skip the Pharmacy
cards.alt: Five signs to skip the pharmacy and go straight to an emergency room: difficulty breathing, chest pain or pressure, neurological changes such as slurred speech, severe pain or injury, and any fever in an infant under three months

items.label: Difficulty breathing
items.note: Wheezing, gasping, or no full breath

items.label: Chest pain or pressure
items.note: Squeezing, or spreading to arm or jaw

items.label: Severe pain or injury
items.note: Bleeding you cannot stop, a deformed limb

items.label: High fever
items.note: Any fever in an infant under three months

cards.subject: Burn
cards.heading: When to Seek Professional Wound Care
title: When a
Burn
Needs the ER
cards.alt: Five signs a burn needs emergency care: it is on the face, hands, feet or a major joint, it is larger than three inches, blisters are numerous or the pain is unmanageable, it is chemical or electrical, or there is difficulty breathing after a fire

items.label: A sensitive location
items.note: Face, hands, feet, genitals or a major joint

items.label: Chemical or electrical
items.note: Damage can hide deep under the skin

items.label: Difficulty breathing
items.note: Smoke or airway burns are life-threatening

cards.subject: dehydration
cards.heading: Spotting the Signs Early
title: Spotting
Dehydration
at the Match
cards.alt: Early dehydration signs in adult fans against young fans: extreme thirst and a dry mouth against a dry tongue and lips, dark urine against fewer than six wet diapers, fatigue or brain fog against listlessness or irritability, and dizziness against no tears when crying

cards.subject: CO Alarm
cards.heading: Why CO Detectors Save Lives
title: Your
CO Alarm
Checklist
cards.alt: A carbon monoxide alarm checklist: place one on every level of the home and one right outside every sleeping area, then test each alarm monthly, change the batteries every six months and replace the unit after five to seven years

good.heading: Where they go
items: One on every level of the home
One right outside every sleeping area

bad.heading: Keeping them working
items: Replace the unit after 5 to 7 years

cards.subject: workplace injury
cards.heading: First Steps: What to Do the Moment an Injury Occurs
title: First Steps After a
Workplace Injury
cards.alt: The first three steps after a workplace injury: call 911 for heavy bleeding or loss of consciousness, get driven to an ER for serious injuries that are not life-threatening, and report the injury to your employer in writing

steps.label: Call 911
steps.note: Heavy bleeding, loss of consciousness, trouble breathing

steps.label: Get to an ER
steps.note: Serious but not life-threatening: have a coworker drive

steps.label: Tell your employer
steps.note: In writing. Texas allows 30 days, but do it the same day

cards.subject: gout
cards.heading: Why Gout Usually Hits at Night
title: Why
Gout
Strikes at Night
cards.alt: Three reasons gout attacks begin between midnight and 8 AM: body temperature drops and uric acid is less soluble when cooler, overnight fluid loss concentrates uric acid, and cortisol is at its lowest

items.label: Your body cools down
items.note: Uric acid is less soluble at lower temperatures

items.label: You lose fluid overnight
items.note: Breathing and sweating concentrate uric acid

items.label: Cortisol is at its lowest
items.note: The hormone that suppresses inflammation dips

cards.subject: dehydration
cards.heading: What Happens If You Are Dehydrated
title: What Untreated
Dehydration
Does
cards.alt: Four things untreated dehydration can lead to: electrolyte imbalance affecting heart rhythm, heat exhaustion or heat stroke above 104 degrees Fahrenheit, kidney strain that can cause stones or acute injury, and hypovolemic shock

items.label: Electrolyte imbalance
items.note: Sodium, potassium and magnesium fall out of balance

items.label: Heat exhaustion or heat stroke
items.note: Heat stroke means a temperature above 104°F

items.label: Kidney strain
items.note: Can lead to stones or acute kidney injury
